subject: Clarify: use of customer text for model training & deletion receipts

Subject: Clarification needed: training use & retention/deletion receipts

Hi Dylan,

Hope you’re well. As part of our procurement security review we need a clear written answer on two items before we can proceed to legal:

1) Do you use customer-provided text (API input, file uploads, chat transcripts) to train or fine-tune any of Redwood’s models (either internal foundation models or fine-tuning pipelines)?
2) Our policy requires an auditable deletion path and a deletion receipt for customer data (we need proof that data was erased from primary stores and backups within a contractual window). Can you describe Redwood’s retention tiers (live logs, backups, snapshots) and the operational process to produce a deletion receipt? We need timings (SLA) and evidence types.

If you can point me to a short attestation or provide a one-page clause we can insert into the SOW, that would help speed things up.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Security Ops
Finovate Payments

Hi Elena,

Short answer up front: we do not use customer-provided text to train or fine-tune our models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a written agreement. I’ll expand below and attach a draft clause and a simple diagram of our retention tiers.

Training usage
- Default (no opt-in): Customer text (API payloads, files, chat logs) is excluded from any training or model-improvement pipelines. Operations and R&D cannot use identifiable customer content for model training.
- Opt-in path: If a customer explicitly agrees to share data for improvement, we require a contract amendment and documented scope (datasets, redaction rules, duration).

Retention & deletion (overview)
- Live logs / request payloads: retained for 30 days by default in primary stores for routing/troubleshooting.
- Short-term backups: rolling backup snapshots retained up to 90 days for disaster recovery.
- Long-term snapshots / archival copies: created only for customer-requested exports or regulatory holds; retention and location are contractually scoped.
- Debug snapshots (tombstones): when debugging, engineers may create short-lived debug snapshots — these are immutable, access-controlled, and deleted within 14 days unless expressly preserved by a customer request.

Deletion receipts & evidence
- Process: customer initiates deletion (API or support ticket) → ops confirms removal from primary stores → automatic background job expunges eligible backups/snapshots per TTL → ops generates a signed deletion report with timestamps and record ids.
- Evidence we provide: export of deletion operations (log ids), S3 object delete markers / tombstone records, and an ops-signed statement with timestamps.
- SLA: standard removal from primary stores within 48 hours; full backup/snapshot purging depends on snapshot schedules but we’ll include a contractual window (commonly 90–120 days) or offer an accelerated purge option for higher-tier contracts.

I’m attaching: 1) draft-non-training-clause.docx (proposed contract language) and 2) redwood-dataflow-diagram.png showing where customer text flows and where retention controls apply. If you want a formal attestation letter we can produce one and have it signed by our Security Officer.

Next steps: would you like the attestation as a standalone PDF or inserted as a clause in the SOW? If Finovate needs a shorter deletion-receipt template, we can provide that as well.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Dylan — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/security team:

1) Our regulator requires a 180-day erase window for certain transaction logs. You mentioned 90–120 days for backups — can we contractually guarantee accelerated purge for covered data (i.e., ensure backups are scrubbed within 180 days)?
2) For deletion receipts: we need a machine-readable proof (JSON log with delete ops and checksums) that we can store in our compliance system. Can Redwood generate that automatically as part of the deletion flow?
3) Regarding training: please confirm that debug snapshots are not routed into any model improvement pipelines even in aggregate form. Some vendors say they aggregate telemetry, which is fine, but Finovate requires assurance that actual customer text does not end up in corp training corpora.

If you can produce a short attestation and an example deletion receipt (redacted) that would expedite sign-off.

Best,
Elena

Elena —

Thanks — good questions. Answers below and I’ve attached a sample (redacted) deletion receipt and a signed SLA PDF for your countersignature.

1) Backup purge window: yes, we can contractually commit to a 180-day maximum for the backup/snapshot purge for regulated transaction logs. For customers who require faster purge we offer an accelerated purge add-on (30–90 days) with a short ops lead time to scrub backups and rehydrate services. We’ll include explicit language in the SOW and the SLA.

2) Machine-readable deletion receipts: we can produce a JSON-based deletion record that includes: delete operation id, affected object keys, timestamps (UTC), deletion job run ids, and a signature/hash from our ops service. Example attached: deletion-receipt-example.json (redacted). We will deliver that automatically after ops confirms all relevant storage tiers are cleared; receipts are archived in your tenant’s compliance folder for 12 months (or configurable).

3) Debug snapshots & model improvement: debug snapshots and any customer-identifiable text are strictly excluded from model training pipelines. Operational telemetry used for model debugging is anonymized and aggregated at a metrics level; raw text is never ingested into training corpora unless there is an explicit opt-in. Our R&D training pipelines only use curated datasets from open sources or opt-in customer data that has been contractually approved.

Operational flow for deletion (summary):
- Customer requests deletion (API ticket) → tracking id created → primary store expunged (48h) → background jobs queue backup purges (within contractual window) → ops validates with deletion job ids → system issues machine-readable receipt → security signs attestation if requested.

I’ve attached: Finovate_Signed_SLA.pdf (placeholder for countersignature) and a redacted deletion-receipt-example.json plus the draft clause. If you’d like, Karthik can set up an HLR with your security team and we can walk through the exact receipt fields and retention timelines.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
